_about: Government schemes that can fund the interventions named by the waterbody rules (rules.json), and the farm-pond schemes behind the 'recent ponds' count. Each scheme keeps the id it has in knowledge/schemes.json (the watershed atlas) where it exists there. 'states' limits a scheme to waterbodies in those states (null = all states). Each link says which of the rule's interventions the scheme can fund; 'types' optionally limits a link to some waterbody types. Status notes were checked on the date in 'verified' and should be checked again before use: scheme names, periods and guidelines change.

schemes.name: Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G)
components: desilting and bund repair (as wage works)
schemes.status: In force since 1 July 2026; replaces MGNREGS
schemes.status_note: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 came into force on 1 July 2026 and repealed the Mahatma Gandhi NREGA, 2005. It guarantees 125 days of wage work (up from 100). Its 'water security' priority area covers water conservation structures, irrigation support, groundwater recharge and rejuvenation of water bodies. Whether desilting and farm ponds are listed by name in the new schedules was not confirmed; check the state's works list. Works are planned through the gram panchayat.

schemes.name: Mission Amrit Sarovar (Phase II)
schemes.department: Ministry of Rural Development (with Jal Shakti and other ministries)
components: new ponds of 1 acre or more
user groups that maintain the pond and remove silt after each monsoon
fishery and other uses by user groups
schemes.status_note: More than 68,000 Amrit Sarovars were completed by March 2025 against a target of 50,000. Phase II continues with a focus on water availability and community participation. It has no budget of its own: works are funded through VB-G RAM G (earlier MGNREGS), 15th Finance Commission grants, the PMKSY watershed component, CSR and crowdfunding. User groups, mostly from SHGs, maintain the ponds and remove silt after each monsoon.

schemes.name: Repair, Renovation and Restoration (RRR) of water bodies, under PMKSY - Har Khet Ko Pani
schemes.department: Ministry of Jal Shakti (with the state water resources / minor irrigation department)
schemes.status: Approved for 2021-26; check whether extended beyond March 2026
schemes.status_note: RRR is a component of PMKSY-HKKP, which was approved for 2021-26. Guidelines (2022) target water bodies with a culturable command area of about 40 ha and above (smaller in hilly and special-category areas), proposed by the state. Small farm ponds and village ponds are generally below its size range; it fits onstream tanks and larger canal-fed tanks.

schemes.name: PMKSY - Command Area Development and Water Management (CAD&WM)
schemes.status: Approved for 2021-26; check whether extended beyond March 2026
schemes.status_note: Part of PMKSY-HKKP. Fits canal-fed waterbodies and the commands of larger tanks, where the problem is water distribution rather than storage.

schemes.name: PMKSY - Per Drop More Crop (micro-irrigation)
schemes.department: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
schemes.status_note: Helps farmers use stored pond water efficiently, which matters where a pond holds water but little rabi crop is grown around it.

schemes.name: PMKSY - Watershed Development Component (WDC 2.0)
schemes.status_note: Fits where the catchment is eroding (silt) or where runoff no longer reaches the waterbody.

schemes.name: Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (incl. Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari)
schemes.status: Active campaign; Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari 2.0 under way in 2026
schemes.status_note: A convergence campaign rather than a funded scheme: works are funded through VB-G RAM G (earlier MGNREGS), Atal Bhujal, 15th Finance Commission grants and CSR. Rajasthan, for example, was fast-tracking Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari 2.0 works (restoration of lakes and ponds, recharge structures) before the 2026 monsoon.

schemes.name: Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal)
schemes.status: Verify current period and covered blocks
schemes.status_note: Covers selected water-stressed blocks of seven states, including Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh among the atlas states. Check whether the block is covered.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
components: new and renovated ponds for inland aquaculture
schemes.status: Active; Rs 2,500 crore in BE 2026-27 (end year not confirmed)
schemes.status_note: Launched in 2020 for five years; it still had a budget allocation of Rs 2,500 crore in 2026-27. In its first six years it supported about 23,285 ha of ponds for inland aquaculture and about 52,000 reservoir cages. Check the current guidelines for the inland pond components.

schemes.name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
schemes.status_note: SHGs often form the Amrit Sarovar user groups and can take up fishery in village ponds.

schemes.name: Gaal-mukt Dharan, Gaal-yukt Shivar (silt-free dams, silt-rich fields)
schemes.department: Soil and Water Conservation Department, Maharashtra
components: desilting of tanks and small dams
schemes.status_note: Still reported in use in 2025-26 (for example, silt spread on farmland in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar). Separately, in June 2026 Maharashtra revised its policy for desilting large irrigation dams, with silt sold to farmers; that policy is for dams, which this atlas leaves out as reservoirs.

schemes.name: Jalyukt Shivar Abhiyan 2.0
schemes.department: Soil and Water Conservation Department, Maharashtra
components: cement nala bunds and repair of old structures
schemes.status_note: The state government ordered water conservation works under Jalyukt Shivar 2.0 to be done on a war footing ahead of an expected El Niño year.

schemes.name: Magel Tyala Shettale (farm ponds on demand)
Mukhyamantri Jal Swavlamban Abhiyan 2.0
schemes.department: Watershed Development and Soil Conservation, Rajasthan
schemes.status_note: Recent reports on Rajasthan's water conservation drive name Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari 2.0 rather than MJSA 2.0; check which one the district is using.

schemes.name: Rajasthan farm pond (khet talai) and diggi subsidy
Khet Talab Yojana
Neelambar-Pitambar Jal Samriddhi Yojana
schemes.status_note: Ran on MGNREGS funds; check how it continues under VB-G RAM G.
